title: delurio domain graph (domain.yaml)
description: The data and the API of a delurio-graph/0 graph (SPEC.md §5): entities whose fields are JSON Schema (2020-12) with delurio's keywords, actions that are OpenAPI 3.1 operations when they have a route, their refusals, the policies that say who may do what to which data, and the invariants that must always hold.

kind.description: The kind of graph file. A domain.yaml is `domain`.

id.description: The domain's id; a flow names it with `domain:`.

title.description: The domain in plain words, for people.

summary.description: What the domain covers, in a few plain sentences.

openapi.description: The OpenAPI document the app already publishes, relative to this file; each action then names its operation by `operationId` instead of copying it.

entities.description: The data, by entity name. An entity is the JSON Schema `{ type: object, properties: <fields>, required: <required> }`.

policies.description: Who may do what to which data (delurio's own: no standard says it).

actions.description: The API and the steps inside the service, by action name. An action with a `route` is one OpenAPI 3.1 operation whose operationId is its name; one with no route is a step inside the service. An action may be named before it is written (an empty value).

invariants.description: What must always hold (delurio's own: no standard says it).

formatVersion.description: The format and its version. Every graph file starts with it.

status.description: `proposed`: written before or apart from the code, nobody has approved it. `captured`: read from existing code (capture mode, every element carries `source`). `approved`: the owner reviewed and accepted it.

sourceAnchor.description: A source anchor (SPEC.md §9): `<repo-relative path>:<line>`, or a bare `<path>` for a whole file, naming the code that makes the element true. In capture mode every element carries one.

fields.description: The entity's fields, by name, each a JSON Schema (2020-12) with delurio's keywords.

required.description: The fields that must be present.

key.description: The fields that identify the entity; `[id]` when left out.

lifecycle.description: The entity's states, as `from -> to: why` sentences. Quote each: an unquoted item that contains `: ` is read as a map.

field.description: A field: a JSON Schema (2020-12) with delurio's keywords (`references`, `unique`, `sensitivity`). `null` is a type like any other: an optional time is `{ type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }`.

schema.description: A JSON Schema (2020-12) with delurio's keywords, or `true` (any value) or `false` (none).

schemaObject.description: A JSON Schema (2020-12) with delurio's keywords.

keywords.description: The keywords of JSON Schema 2020-12 (core, applicator, unevaluated, validation, meta-data, format and content vocabularies), and the keywords delurio adds, which a JSON Schema validator leaves alone.

$schema.description: JSON Schema: the dialect of the schema.

$ref.description: JSON Schema: a reference to another schema.

$anchor.description: JSON Schema: a plain-name fragment for this schema.

$dynamicRef.description: JSON Schema: a reference resolved in the dynamic scope.

$defs.description: JSON Schema: schemas kept for `$ref`, by name.

$comment.description: JSON Schema: a comment for the schema's authors.

allOf.description: JSON Schema: the value is valid against every one of these.

anyOf.description: JSON Schema: the value is valid against at least one of these.

oneOf.description: JSON Schema: the value is valid against exactly one of these.

not.description: JSON Schema: the value is not valid against this.

if.description: JSON Schema: when the value is valid against this, `then` applies, else `else`.

else.description: JSON Schema: applies when `if` does not hold.

dependentSchemas.description: JSON Schema: per property name, a schema that applies when the property is present.

prefixItems.description: JSON Schema: the schemas of the first items, in order.

items.description: JSON Schema: the schema of every item (after `prefixItems`).

contains.description: JSON Schema: at least one item is valid against this.

properties.description: JSON Schema: the schema of each property, by name. delurio's keywords may be used on each.

patternProperties.description: JSON Schema: per regular expression, the schema of the properties whose names match it.

additionalProperties.description: JSON Schema: the schema of the properties not named in `properties` or `patternProperties`.

propertyNames.description: JSON Schema: the schema every property name is valid against.

unevaluatedItems.description: JSON Schema: the schema of the items no other keyword evaluated.

unevaluatedProperties.description: JSON Schema: the schema of the properties no other keyword evaluated.

type.description: JSON Schema: the value's type, or a list of types. `null` is a type like any other.

const.description: JSON Schema: the only value allowed.

enum.description: JSON Schema: the values allowed. An enum that may be empty lists `null` among its values.

multipleOf.description: JSON Schema: the number is a multiple of this.

maximum.description: JSON Schema: the largest number allowed.

exclusiveMaximum.description: JSON Schema: the number is less than this.

minimum.description: JSON Schema: the smallest number allowed.

exclusiveMinimum.description: JSON Schema: the number is greater than this.

maxLength.description: JSON Schema: the longest string allowed, in characters.

minLength.description: JSON Schema: the shortest string allowed, in characters.

pattern.description: JSON Schema: a regular expression (ECMA-262) the string matches.

maxItems.description: JSON Schema: the most items allowed.

minItems.description: JSON Schema: the fewest items allowed.

uniqueItems.description: JSON Schema: `true` when no two items may be equal.

maxContains.description: JSON Schema: the most items valid against `contains`.

minContains.description: JSON Schema: the fewest items valid against `contains`.

maxProperties.description: JSON Schema: the most properties allowed.

minProperties.description: JSON Schema: the fewest properties allowed.

required.description: JSON Schema: the properties that must be present.

dependentRequired.description: JSON Schema: per property name, the properties that must be present when it is.

description.description: JSON Schema: what the value is, in words.

default.description: JSON Schema: the value when none is given.

deprecated.description: JSON Schema: `true` when the value should no longer be used.

readOnly.description: JSON Schema: `true` when the value is set by the service, never by the caller.

writeOnly.description: JSON Schema: `true` when the value is sent but never answered back.

format.description: JSON Schema: a format of the string.

contentEncoding.description: JSON Schema: how the string encodes binary content.

contentMediaType.description: JSON Schema: the media type of the string's content.

contentSchema.description: JSON Schema: the schema of the string's decoded content.

references.description: delurio: the field holds the key of this other entity.

unique.description: delurio: no two entities have the same value: `true`, or `case-insensitive`.

sensitivity.description: delurio: what may be shown, logged or kept. `credential`: never shown, logged or stored in clear. `personal`: data about a person. `internal`: never shown to users.

owner.description: delurio, capture only: a word the capture keeps on a field; no tool reads it.

note.description: delurio, capture only: a word the capture keeps on a field; no tool reads it.

editableBy.description: delurio, capture only: a word the capture keeps on a field; no tool reads it.

matching.description: delurio, capture only: a word the capture keeps on a field (how values are compared, e.g. `exact`); no tool reads it.

opaque.description: delurio, capture only: a word the capture keeps on a field (the value is passed on unread); no tool reads it.

action.description: An action. With a `route` it is one OpenAPI 3.1 operation: its name is the operationId, `needs` its security requirement, `query` its query parameters, `body` its request body, `result` its response, and each refusal one more response.

route.description: `METHOD /path`: the HTTP method and the path of the operation. An action with no route is a step inside the service.

operationId.description: The operation in the app's own OpenAPI document (named at the top with `openapi:`), when it is not this action's name.

summary.description: OpenAPI: the operation in a few words.

description.description: OpenAPI: what the operation or the step does, in words.

needs.description: delurio: what the caller must hold (the operation's security requirement).

query.description: The query parameters: a JSON Schema object.

body.description: The request body: a JSON Schema.

refusals.description: Each way the action refuses, by refusal code; each is one more response of the operation. A flow's `failures` sort the codes into classes.

sideEffects.description: delurio: what else the action does, each in words or as `<kind>:<event>`.

note.description: The author's own words about the action, which no tool reads (SPEC.md §5).

result.description: The action's response: `returns` an entity, a `redirect`, a `status`, or a JSON Schema.

redirect.description: Where the response redirects, in words or as a path.

status.description: The HTTP status of the response.

refusal.description: A refusal: one more response of the operation.

status.description: The HTTP status of the refusal.

redirect.description: delurio: whether and where the refusal redirects, e.g. `never` (a page is shown), `error` (back to the caller with the error), `retry`, or a path.

body.description: The refusal's body: RFC 9457 problem details whose `type` is the refusal code.

note.description: The author's own words about the refusal, which no tool reads (SPEC.md §5).

policy.description: Who may do what to which data.

where.description: The condition under which it holds, in words.

read.description: The entities the actor may read.

write.description: The entities the actor may write.

do.description: The actions the actor may invoke.

spec.description: The standard and section it comes from, cited, never written again.

holds.description: `false` when the code does not keep the invariant: it is still written, as what should hold, with the `finding` that says where it does not. `true` when left out.

finding.description: The finding that reports where the code breaks the invariant: its id in the graph's report. Required with `holds: false`.

note.description: The author's own words about the invariant, which no tool reads (SPEC.md §5).

allOf.$comment: an invariant the code does not keep names the finding that reports it
